title: Compatibility-first BUILD-C spine and durable boundary-first PROVE
summary: Bind the consolidated program to governed v2.17.16, close R-0009 as no-build evidence, add exactly six live R-0010 BUILD-C gaps over incumbent command/review/worktree primitives, then re-deliver donor surfaces through a durable seven-part R-0011 PROVE.

current_state.summary: At exact HEAD bba3354e7fc5eb052beac74af230611ae48bd7db (v2.17.16, tree a7f46dbf6859f7d2122c4ee6ce99006b4862197a), public CLI and loop roots already call the governed command engine, which composes durable CommandRuntime and CommandAdapter owners. Event waits are 1800-second wake-only/non-polling, automatic review selects exactly 4–5 concurrent quick lenses including architecture, and automatic deep is refused because a direct-human command is not shipped. Existing graph/worktree/merge-receipt/review/evidence/enforcement primitives are reusable. loop.submit has no AC checkpoint, Design approval has no DEFINE ReviewKernel call, default parallel Build uses wave/claim/stage-split state, merge lacks checkpoint-SHA authorization, and the R-0011 prove/tier/registry modules, frozen inventory, exports, and exact 23 tests are absent. The engine inventory is empty, so these facts are grounded in the cited sources and exact Git objects.

alternatives.name: Compatibility-first checkpoint spine
alternatives.description: Record v2.17.16 without code change, add only six missing BUILD-C live edges over incumbent boundaries, then re-deliver donor content through the proven spine and durable PROVE.

gains: Preserves event waits, bounded review, graph/worktree identity, and receipts
Makes every new behavior positive- and severed-edge testable
Keeps donor history as source evidence only
costs: R-0011 waits for exact pushed-SHA proof and sign-off
tradeoffs.revisit_when: A baseline-positive capability fails a live reuse fixture, or a seventh gap is proven and a human expands Product scope.

alternatives.name: Donor first, BUILD-C retrofit
alternatives.description: Port later boundary-first surfaces first and add checkpointing/reconciliation afterward.

gains: Source layout is familiar from later history
tradeoffs.revisit_when: Only under a replacement requirement explicitly authorizing later-history implementation input.

alternatives.name: New orchestration core
alternatives.description: Replace runtime, router, worktree, receipt, and proof paths with a greenfield scheduler and evidence service.

tradeoffs.revisit_when: Multiple incumbent contracts fail production compatibility and Product authorizes platform redesign.

alternatives.name: Verification-only status quo
alternatives.description: Record v2.17.16 and stop after R-0009.

decision: Select the compatibility-first checkpoint spine because it alone satisfies the authoritative baseline, six-gap scope, predecessor gates, reuse invariants, live-edge rule, and donor-as-source-only boundary. Two new R-0010 owners compose incumbent runtime/review/graph/worktree contracts; three new R-0011 proof owners make exact-identity PROVE the sole completion evidence.

risks.risk: A baseline-positive capability is accidentally reimplemented.
risks.mitigation: Closed reuse matrix plus six-category Plan readiness and differential golden fixtures reject the task before Build.

risks.risk: Caller-authored checkpoint fields impersonate engine evidence.
risks.mitigation: Checkpoint accepts only CommandRuntime/Git-derived fields, rejects unknown observed fields, and binds engine/contract/command/environment/output/result/revision digests.

risks.risk: A green receipt authorizes another worktree revision.
risks.mitigation: Integration authorization requires equality among checkpoint target SHA, registered worktree tip, predecessor receipts, assignment scope, and merge receipt.

risks.risk: Legacy wave/claim/lease state leaks into thin BUILD.
risks.mitigation: Direct mode has a closed state schema and asserts zero forbidden records; governed-build remains separate and retained.

risks.risk: Later donor history is imported as proof.
risks.mitigation: Path/content provenance is separated from Git authority; ancestry and diff checks reject v2.17.17+ parents, cherry-picks, and receipts.

risks.risk: PROVE components attest different revisions or plans.
risks.mitigation: One canonical identity set is validated before collection and every component receipt repeats its digest; mixed evidence fails.

risks.risk: A restart overwrites red or partial proof.
risks.mitigation: Append-only attempt ids and predecessor digests preserve every event; resume may only continue the same open attempt.

risks.risk: New Python modules or registry data are omitted from plugin packages.
risks.mitigation: Strict typing, support-matrix compile/import, deterministic package contents, clean installed-plugin smoke, and archive provenance checks are blocking.

failure_modes.recovery: Program owner corrects the local evidence selection or returns to Product in the same R-0009 attempt; no executable state is created.

failure_modes.mode: Focused proof is absent, fails, is canceled/dies, or targets a stale revision.
failure_modes.detection: signal:r0012.checkpoint names AC, file, command, revision, terminal condition, and stopped phase.
failure_modes.recovery: Task owner repairs only the declared AC scope and runs a new checkpoint on a new exact revision; no later phase or integration runs.

failure_modes.mode: Checkpoint evidence is forged, truncated where completeness is required, or identity-mixed.
failure_modes.recovery: Checkpoint owner discards caller data and re-derives one receipt from the durable runtime journal within the same checkpoint attempt.

failure_modes.mode: DEFINE/final review emits invalid depth, count, architecture, concurrency, or wait.
failure_modes.detection: signal:r0012.review-projection reports the boundary and invalid selector/manifest field.
failure_modes.recovery: Orchestration owner corrects the incumbent-router invocation and restarts that projection; zero Plan/sign-off authority is created.

failure_modes.mode: Assignment overlaps, escapes scope, or has ambiguous identity.
failure_modes.detection: signal:r0012.assignment names the tasks, canonical scopes, overlap/out-of-scope path, and graph identity.
failure_modes.recovery: BUILD-C serializes valid overlap automatically or the planner obtains a corrected approved Plan before redispatch; no affected branch integrates.

failure_modes.mode: Integration receives red, stale, or dependency-incomplete work.
failure_modes.detection: signal:r0012.integration reports checkpoint digest, registered tip, predecessor status, and refusal.
failure_modes.recovery: Orchestrator retains the worktree and waits for one new green exact-tip checkpoint; dependents remain isolated and are never rebased onto red.

failure_modes.mode: Tier, schema, reconciliation, or canary proof fails.
failure_modes.detection: signal:r0012.tier-registry or signal:r0012.reconciliation names the missing/test/schema/module/canary condition.
failure_modes.recovery: Non-builder evaluator permits the one checkpointed batch fix, then PROVE reruns all seven components on a new exact revision.

failure_modes.mode: A PROVE component is missing, mixed, duplicate, partial, or second-red.
failure_modes.detection: signal:r0012.prove-component and signal:r0012.prove-attempt report component, attempt, identity, durable predecessor, and limit.
failure_modes.recovery: Proof owner resumes the open attempt or starts the one allowed complete re-PROVE; second red blocks and returns an attributed human action.

failure_modes.mode: An external action lacks its own approval.
failure_modes.detection: signal:r0012.external-action names the action class, exact target, and missing/mismatched approval.
failure_modes.recovery: Release owner obtains a distinct prior attributed approval or leaves only that action unperformed; local evidence remains valid.

rollout.strategy: After one attributed consolidated Design approval, record no-build R-0009 baseline/reuse evidence; bootstrap R-0010 manually in checkpoint/receipt, submit wiring, DEFINE, direct assignment, merge authorization, then compatibility/live-edge order; require separate authorized push, exact fetched-SHA proof, and human R-0010 sign-off; re-deliver R-0011 in the eight catalog groups through R-0010, then run final review, complete PROVE, Retro, and separately approved external actions.
rollout.rollback: Before sharing, abandon local code-bearing branches and return to unchanged bba3354e while retaining/superseding evidence append-safely. Direct BUILD-C remains disabled until green and existing governed-build stays intact; red R-0010 keeps R-0011 closed. After sharing, correct forward or disable the delivery mode—never reset, force-push, move tags, delete receipts, or mutate donor evidence. Failed R-0011 PROVE keeps durable attempts and blocks sign-off.

visualization.reason: The no-build R-0009 closure, manually bootstrapped R-0010, exact-SHA/human boundary, R-0011 one-fix PROVE loop, and independent external actions form an ordered failure-sensitive state machine that is materially clearer visually.
